articles.title: Mark Cuban's Cost-Plus Enters New Jersey Employer Benefits Market
articles.summary: Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company is expanding its pharmacy benefits model into New Jersey's employer market, intensifying competition against traditional PBMs. This move offers self-funded employers alternative pricing structures focused on transparency and direct-to-consumer cost savings. The entry signals continued disruption in the PBM space as employers seek non-traditional partners to manage rising drug expenditures.

articles.title: Insurer-Owned PBMs Lose Ground in Commercial Health Plan Market
articles.summary: Insurer-owned pharmacy benefit managers are experiencing a decline in market share within the commercial sector as employers increasingly seek alternatives. This shift highlights growing employer dissatisfaction with traditional integrated PBM models and creates opportunities for independent, transparent PBM alternatives.

articles.title: Rebates Rise While Self-Funded Pharmacy Costs Climb
articles.summary: The article examines the disconnect between increasing pharmaceutical manufacturer rebates and the ongoing rise in overall employer-sponsored pharmacy plan costs. This dynamic directly impacts self-funded employers struggling to manage net drug spend despite traditional PBM rebate guarantees. The key implication is that employers must look beyond headline rebates and scrutinize underlying pricing structures and PBM alignment to truly control specialty and total pharmacy expenditures.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:07:24 GMT

articles.title: Congressional PBM Reform Faces Hurdles Before Reaching Consumers
articles.summary: The article discusses ongoing legislative efforts surrounding pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) reform and the challenges Congress faces in passing impactful measures that directly benefit consumers and plan sponsors. This is strategically important for self-funded employers and PBMs monitoring federal policy shifts, transparency demands, and potential regulatory changes to drug pricing models.

articles.title: Optum Rx and Express Scripts Extend Market Lead Over Rival PBMs
articles.summary: Recent data highlights that Optum Rx and Express Scripts have further cemented their dominant market share positions within the pharmacy benefit management industry. This consolidation of power among the largest PBMs impacts the competitive landscape for self-funded employers seeking alternatives for transparent, cost-effective benefit management.
articles.source_line: Source: Modern Healthcare; Tue, 06 Oct 2026 16:00:00 GMT

articles.title: Judge Stays Public Nuisance Lawsuit Against Major PBMs
articles.summary: A federal judge has agreed to stay a public nuisance case targeting major pharmacy benefit managers. This litigation pause impacts ongoing legal challenges surrounding PBM business practices and pricing models, which are of high strategic interest to self-funded employers monitoring industry accountability.

articles.title: Rewriting the Post-Exclusivity Playbook for Generics and Biosimilars
articles.summary: The article examines how the pharmaceutical market is evolving post-exclusivity for major drugs, focusing on strategies for generics and biosimilars. This is critically important for self-funded employers and PBMs looking to leverage biosimilar adoption and generic competition to drive down surging specialty and prescription drug costs. The implication is a shifting formulary landscape that requires active management to maximize savings from upcoming patent cliffs.

articles.title: McKesson and CD&R Acquire Option Care Health for $5.8 Billion
articles.summary: McKesson and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice have agreed to acquire infusion services provider Option Care Health in a $5.8 billion deal. This major consolidation in specialty healthcare impacts the specialty pharmacy landscape, which is critical for self-funded employers managing high-cost specialty drug spend.

articles.title: PharmaForce Launches Connected 340B Rebate and MFP Solution
articles.summary: PharmaForce has introduced an integrated solution designed to manage 340B rebates and the Maximum Fair Price (MFP) program. This technology impacts drug pricing operations and compliance within the pharmacy supply chain, which directly affects PBM operations and stakeholder cost management.
articles.source_line: Source: Business Wire; Tue, 06 Oct 2026 18:03:00 GMT

articles.title: Rising Hospital and Drug Costs Threaten Self-Funded Employer Health Plans
articles.summary: Soaring medical and pharmaceutical prices are placing an unsustainable financial burden on American businesses sponsoring self-funded health plans. The pressure highlights the urgent need for employers to implement aggressive cost-management strategies and PBM transparency measures.
articles.source_line: Source: Word & Brown General Agency; Tue, 06 Oct 2026 17:05:21 GMT
